title: 공원 가기
intro: 설문에서 '공원 가기'를 고르면 자주 가는 공원 묘사 → 공원에서 하는 일·루틴 → 기억에 남는 공원 경험 → 어릴 때 공원과 지금 공원 비교가 거의 정해진 순서로 나옵니다. 혼자 사는 아파트에서 걸어서 5분 거리인 작은 동네 공원(퇴근 후 산책, 주말 벤치 독서)과 자전거로 10분인 한강공원(조깅, 피크닉) 두 곳을 고정해 두고 모든 질문에 재활용하세요. 비교 질문은 대전 본가 아파트 놀이터 옆 공원을 과거 장면으로 씁니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, parks? Sure, I go to the park near my place all the time.' 같은 시작 문장 → 어디에 있는 어떤 공원인지 → 무엇이 보이는지(산책로, 나무, 벤치) → 왜 좋은지(조용함, 스트레스 해소) → 'Yeah, that's why I love going to the park.' 마무리 문장.
공원 묘사는 위치(집에서 걸어서 5분) → 크기 → 눈에 보이는 것 3가지(산책로·벤치·작은 놀이터) → 사람들(강아지 산책, 운동하는 사람) 순서로 공간을 훑듯이 말합니다.
루틴·경험 질문은 퇴근 후 산책, 주말 아이스 아메리카노 + 벤치 독서, 한강 조깅·피크닉처럼 페르소나 일상과 바로 연결합니다.
IH 이상은 대전 어린 시절 공원(모래 놀이터, 남동생 Junho) vs 지금 공원(산책로·운동기구·야간 조명·푸드트럭) 비교와 'clear my head' 같은 쉬운 관용 표현을 더합니다.

expressions.en: Oh, parks? Sure, I go to the park near my place all the time.
expressions.ko: 아, 공원이요? 네, 저는 집 근처 공원에 자주 가요.
expressions.note: 시작 문장: my place = 우리 집 (구어체로 자주 써요)

expressions.en: There's a small park about five minutes from my apartment.
expressions.ko: 제 아파트에서 5분 정도 거리에 작은 공원이 있어요.
expressions.note: There's ~ + 거리: 장소 묘사 첫 문장으로 최고

expressions.en: There's a walking path that goes around the park.
expressions.ko: 공원을 한 바퀴 도는 산책로가 있어요.

expressions.en: There are a lot of tall trees and benches.
Many people walk their dogs there in the evening.
expressions.ko: 저녁에는 많은 사람들이 거기서 강아지를 산책시켜요.

expressions.en: I usually take a walk in the park after work.
expressions.ko: 저는 보통 퇴근 후 공원에서 산책을 해요.

expressions.en: It's quiet and peaceful, so I can relax there.
expressions.ko: 조용하고 평화로워서 거기서 쉴 수 있어요.

expressions.en: On weekends, I sit on a bench with an iced Americano and read a book.
expressions.ko: 주말에는 아이스 아메리카노를 들고 벤치에 앉아 책을 읽어요.

expressions.en: Walking in the park helps me clear my head after a long day.
expressions.ko: 공원 산책은 긴 하루 뒤에 머리를 맑게 해 줘요.
expressions.note: clear my head: 머리를 식히다, 생각을 정리하다

expressions.en: The Han River park is only ten minutes away by bike.
expressions.note: ~ minutes away by bike / subway: 교통수단별 거리

expressions.en: All of a sudden, it started pouring, so we ran under the bridge.
expressions.ko: 갑자기 비가 쏟아져서 저희는 다리 밑으로 뛰어갔어요.
expressions.note: All of a sudden: 경험 답변에서 반전 시작 신호

expressions.en: When I was a kid, the park near our apartment only had a sandbox and some swings.
expressions.ko: 어렸을 때 우리 아파트 근처 공원에는 모래 놀이터와 그네 몇 개뿐이었어요.
expressions.note: When I was a kid ~: 비교 질문의 과거 장면 시작

expressions.en: It's my little escape from the busy city.
expressions.ko: 그곳은 바쁜 도시에서 벗어나는 저만의 작은 탈출구예요.
expressions.note: escape를 명사로 써서 감정을 담은 묘사

expressions.en: These days, parks are not just places for kids anymore.
expressions.ko: 요즘 공원은 더 이상 아이들만을 위한 곳이 아니에요.
expressions.note: not just ~ anymore: 변화를 강조하는 비교 표현

expressions.en: Yeah, that's why I love going to the park.
expressions.ko: 네, 그래서 저는 공원 가는 걸 좋아해요.
expressions.note: 마무리 문장: 주제 키워드를 넣어 깔끔하게 끝내세요.

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you like going to parks. Tell me about a park you often go to. Where is it, and what does it look like?
questions.ko: 설문에서 공원 가는 것을 좋아한다고 하셨습니다. 자주 가는 공원에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떻게 생겼나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 위치(아파트에서 걸어서 5분) → 크기·모습(산책로, 나무, 벤치, 작은 놀이터) → 사람들 → 좋아하는 이유 → 마무리.
There is / There are 로 보이는 것을 하나씩 나열하면 묘사가 쉬워집니다. 3~4개면 충분해요.
IH 이상은 계절·시간대 모습(봄 벚꽃, 저녁 조명)과 감정('my little escape')을 더하세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, parks? Sure, I go to the park near my place all the time. There's a small park about five minutes from my apartment. It's in a quiet neighborhood. There's a walking path that goes around the park. There are a lot of tall trees and benches. There's also a small playground for kids. In the evening, many people walk their dogs there. It's quiet and peaceful, so I can relax there. Yeah, that's the park I often go to.
answers.IH: Oh, parks? Sure, I go to the park near my place all the time. The park I go to the most is a small neighborhood park about five minutes from my apartment. I live alone near my office in Seoul, and this park is right on my way home from the subway station. It's not very big, but it's really nice. There's a walking path that goes around the whole park, and there are tall trees on both sides. In the middle, there's a small playground and some exercise machines. There are also a lot of benches, so people can sit and rest. In spring, the trees are full of cherry blossoms, and it's really pretty. In the evening, many people walk their dogs or jog there. Yeah, that's the park I often go to.
answers.AL: Oh, parks? Sure, I go to the park near my place all the time, so I can tell you a lot about it. The one I go to the most is a small neighborhood park just five minutes from my apartment. I moved to this area three years ago when I started working, and honestly, this park was one of the reasons I chose my place. It's right between the subway station and my building, so I walk through it almost every day on my way home. It's not huge, but it's really well kept. There's a walking path that loops around the whole park, and it's lined with tall trees on both sides. In the middle, there's a little playground and some outdoor exercise machines, and there are wooden benches everywhere. In spring, the cherry blossoms are absolutely gorgeous, and at night, the soft streetlights make it feel really cozy. In the evening, you can see people walking their dogs, older couples taking a stroll, and office workers like me just trying to unwind. For me, it's my little escape from the busy city. If I want something bigger, the Han River park is only ten minutes away by bike. So yeah, that's the park I often go to.

questions.en: What do you usually do when you go to the park? When do you usually go, and who do you go with?
questions.ko: 공원에 가면 보통 무엇을 하나요? 주로 언제 가고, 누구와 함께 가나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제(평일 퇴근 후, 주말 오후) → 누구와(주로 혼자, 가끔 Minji·친구) → 무엇을(산책·음악, 벤치 독서, 한강 조깅) → 왜 좋은지 → 마무리.
평일 루틴과 주말 루틴을 나눠서 말하면 구조가 깔끔해지고 길이도 자연스럽게 늘어납니다.
IH 이상은 '주 3회 한강 조깅 30분', '근처 카페에서 아이스 아메리카노 사서 벤치 독서' 같은 숫자·구체적 디테일을 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about what I do at the park. I usually go to the park near my apartment after work. I go there about two or three times a week. I usually go alone. I take a walk for about thirty minutes and listen to music. On weekends, I sit on a bench and read a book. Sometimes my friends come, and we walk and talk together. Yeah, that's what I usually do at the park.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about what I usually do at the park. On weekdays, I go to the small park near my apartment after work, about two or three times a week. I usually go alone. I put in my earbuds, listen to some ballads, and walk around the park for about thirty minutes. Walking in the park helps me clear my head after a long day of meetings. On weekends, I go in the afternoon. I buy an iced Americano at a café nearby, and then I sit on a bench and read a book. Sometimes my coworker Minji comes over, and we walk around the park and chat. Also, three times a week, I go jogging at the Han River park, which is ten minutes away by bike. Yeah, that's what I usually do at the park.
answers.AL: Okay, let me tell you about what I usually do at the park, because it's a big part of my routine. On weekdays, I usually stop by the small park near my apartment on my way home from work. I go there two or three times a week, usually around seven, and most of the time I go alone. I put in my earbuds, play some calm ballads, and walk around the park for about thirty minutes. After a whole day of back-to-back meetings, it really helps me clear my head, and by the time I get home, I feel like a different person. On weekends, my routine is a little more relaxing. I sleep in, grab an iced Americano from a café near the park, and then I find a shady bench and read a book for an hour or so. Every now and then, my coworker Minji comes over to my neighborhood, and we walk around the park and chat about everything except work, which is kind of our rule. On top of that, three times a week, I hop on my bike and ride ten minutes to the Han River park to go jogging. Watching the sunset over the river while I run is the best part. So yeah, that's what I usually do at the park.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable experience you had at a park. When was it, who were you with, what happened, and why do you still remember it?
questions.ko: 공원에서 있었던 기억에 남는 경험에 대해 말해 주세요. 언제였고, 누구와 함께 있었으며, 무슨 일이 있었고, 왜 아직도 기억하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·어디서·누구와(작년 봄, 한강공원, Minji와 대학 친구들) → 처음 상황(치킨 배달 피크닉) → 사건(갑자기 소나기, 다리 밑으로 대피) → 결말·느낌 → 마무리.
'All of a sudden ~'으로 반전을 시작하면 이야기에 긴장감이 생깁니다. 과거시제를 끝까지 유지하세요.
IH 이상은 대사 한 줄(작은따옴표)과 '왜 아직 기억하는지' 이유를 꼭 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, a memorable experience? Let me think. Last spring, I went to the Han River park with Minji and some friends. We had a picnic on the grass. We ordered fried chicken, and it was delivered right to the park. But all of a sudden, it started raining. We grabbed our food and ran under the bridge. We were all wet, but we laughed a lot. Then the rain stopped, and we saw a beautiful sunset. Yeah, that's my most memorable day at the park.
answers.IH: Oh, a memorable experience? Let me think. I remember one day really clearly. It was last spring, on a Saturday. My coworker Minji and two of my college friends came to my neighborhood, and we went to the Han River park for a picnic. We set up a mat on the grass, and we ordered fried chicken. It's amazing that you can get food delivered right to the park in Korea. Everything was perfect at first. But all of a sudden, the sky got dark, and it started pouring. We grabbed the chicken and ran under the bridge. We were completely soaked, but we couldn't stop laughing. After about twenty minutes, the rain stopped, and we saw a beautiful sunset over the river. I still remember it because it was such a fun surprise. Yeah, that's my most memorable day at the park.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable experience? Let me think. Actually, there's one day I'll never forget. It was last spring, on a sunny Saturday afternoon. My coworker Minji and two of my college friends came over to my neighborhood, and we decided to have a picnic at the Han River park. We rode bikes there, spread out a mat on the grass, and ordered fried chicken. If you've never tried it, getting chicken delivered right to the riverside is one of the best things about living in Seoul. Everything was perfect. We were eating, chatting, and complaining about our bosses. But then, all of a sudden, the sky turned dark gray, and it started pouring. We grabbed the chicken boxes and sprinted to the bridge as fast as we could. By the time we got there, we were soaked from head to toe, and one of my friends said, 'Well, at least the chicken is safe.' We all burst out laughing, and we just ate the rest of the chicken under the bridge. About twenty minutes later, the rain stopped, and the sky turned pink and orange. It was one of the most beautiful sunsets I've ever seen. I still remember that day because, even though nothing went as planned, it turned out to be perfect. So yeah, that's my most memorable day at the park.

questions.en: How are parks today different from the parks you went to when you were a child? What has changed?
questions.ko: 요즘 공원은 어렸을 때 갔던 공원과 어떻게 다른가요? 무엇이 변했나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 과거(대전 본가 아파트 옆 작은 공원, 모래 놀이터·그네, 남동생 Junho와 놀기) → 현재(넓은 산책로, 운동기구, 야간 조명, 푸드트럭·행사) → 변화에 대한 내 생각 → 마무리.
과거는 used to / back then, 현재는 these days / now 로 확실히 나누고, bigger / cleaner / safer 같은 비교급을 쓰세요.
IH 이상은 '공원 이용자가 아이들 → 모든 연령'으로 바뀌었다는 큰 변화 하나와 이유를 덧붙이면 좋습니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, that's a good question. Let me think. When I was a kid, I lived with my family in Daejeon. There was a small park near our apartment. It only had a sandbox and some swings. I used to play there with my little brother Junho. But parks today are much bigger and cleaner. They have nice walking paths and exercise machines. They also have lights at night, so they're safer. Yeah, parks have changed a lot.
answers.IH: Oh, that's a good question. Let me think. Parks have changed a lot since I was a kid. When I was young, I lived with my family in an old apartment in Daejeon. There was a small park right next to our building, but it was pretty simple. It only had a sandbox, a slide, and some swings. After school, I used to play there with my little brother Junho until my mom called us for dinner. Back then, parks were mostly for kids. But these days, parks are much bigger and nicer. The park near my apartment in Seoul has a long walking path, outdoor exercise machines, and lots of benches. They also have bright lights at night, so I feel safe walking there alone after work. Now, people of all ages use parks to exercise and relax. Yeah, that's how parks have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, that's a good question. Let me think. I'd say parks have changed a lot since I was a kid. When I was little, I lived with my family in an old apartment in Daejeon, and there was a tiny park right next to our building. Honestly, it was nothing special. It had a sandbox, a rusty slide, and a couple of swings, and that was pretty much it. Still, my little brother Junho and I used to play there every day after school until our mom yelled at us to come home for dinner. Back then, parks were mostly for kids, and adults just sat on the benches and watched. These days, though, parks are not just places for kids anymore. The park near my apartment in Seoul has a long walking path, outdoor exercise machines, and even a small stage for events. The Han River park is on a whole different level. There are bike paths, food trucks, and festivals on weekends. Another big change is safety. Parks today are well lit at night, so as someone who lives alone, I feel totally comfortable taking a walk there after work. I think it's a great change, because now everyone, from kids to office workers like me, can enjoy them. So yeah, that's how parks have changed.

pronunciation.tip: '파크'가 아니라 입을 크게 벌린 '파-r크'. 모음 뒤에 혀를 살짝 말아 r을 넣고, 끝 k는 짧게 끊으세요.
'패스'가 아니라 끝에 th(θ). 혀끝을 이 사이에 살짝 물고 바람만 내보내세요.
강세는 'play'. 'ground'의 gr은 모음 없이 바로 붙여서 '플레이그롸운드'처럼 말합니다.
'스트롤'처럼 모음을 넣지 말고 s-t-r을 한 번에. 끝 l은 혀를 윗잇몸에 대며 '오울'로 마무리하세요.
